name: Concealed corporate subcontracting to DPRK IT workers

attribution.legal_posture: FATF reports an arrest-stage jurisdiction submission and alleged falsification and subcontracting pattern; conviction, final judgment, named parties, and upstream customer or platform complicity remain unreported.

caveats: Monitoring, communications behavior, quota pressure, subcontracting, trading activity, geography, language, and any single signal require corroboration before supporting identity, nationality, sanctions, or misconduct attribution.
Evidence and method class: FATF case study submitted by Japan, describing arrests and investigative findings.
FATF summarizes a jurisdiction submission; the reviewed material omits the charging instrument, final judgment, company names, and complete transaction trail.
Fraudulent employment, general DPRK overseas labor, sanctions evasion, and malicious cyber activity remain analytically distinct unless a cited source expressly connects them.

Publish as an anonymized, allegation-labeled case pattern. Emphasize supplier-chain transparency and subcontractor verification; upstream customer or platform characterization requires direct evidence.
The finding establishes one alleged case pattern; prevalence among software subcontractors or online platforms remains unmeasured.
The Japanese customer is described as a customer; knowing or complicit status remains unassessed.
This record is policy, labor-governance, economic, or sanctions-evasion context; person, organization, victim, account, transaction, and incident profiles require separate records.

infrastructure.evidence_method_class: FATF case study submitted by Japan, describing arrests and investigative findings
infrastructure.statement: FATF reports that in March 2024 a South Korean IT-company president and former employee were arrested after investigators found that records had allegedly been falsified and application-development work ordered by a Japanese company through an online platform had been assigned to DPRK IT workers believed to be in China. The pattern places a foreign corporate intermediary between the customer, platform, and actual workforce.
sampling_limitations: FATF summarizes a jurisdiction submission and does not include the charging instrument, final judgment, company names, or complete transaction trail.
The finding establishes one alleged case pattern, not prevalence among software subcontractors or online platforms.
The Japanese customer is not characterized as knowing or complicit.
